title: Caching and Request Coordination knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Caching and Request Coordination”?
options: Caching and Request Coordination helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Caching and Request Coordination means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Caching and Request Coordination removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Caching and Request Coordination should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Caching and Request Coordination helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Caching and Request Coordination is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Request deduplication” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Request deduplication” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Request deduplication” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Request deduplication” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Request deduplication” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Request deduplication” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Request deduplication” under Caching and Request Coordination. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Caching and Request Coordination”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
